correctness.rationale: Independent proof check: for ranks r,s a product has rank s−dim(im(right)∩ker(left)); subspaces of the prescribed dimensions realize every intersection size between max(0,s−r) and min(s,n−r), and left/right changes of basis realize the entire resulting rank classes. The units do not add conditions: |GL_n(K)|>2 even for n=2 over F₂, so each unit factors into two nonidentity units, and multiplying rank strata by any one unit preserves them bijectively. If a rank block B skips a rank k of C, take a=min B<k<b=max B. The product contains ranks a and k by using factor ranks (a,k) and (b,k). Saturation forces both b and max C into the product; the ranks are bounded above by min(b,max C), giving the impossible b=max C. For interval blocks [a,b],[u,v], any k between max(0,a+u−n) and min(b,v) occurs using max(a,k),max(u,k); both rank constraints follow directly. The right bound is already a block endpoint, so precisely the left bounds must be starts, yielding truncated-addition closure. Reflection around n converts that closure to addition below n, with all sums ≥n included and 0 adjoined. E₁₁ and E₁₂ lie in the same rank-one class but only E₁₁ is idempotent, precluding automorphism orbits.
